Create one linked child programme per genuine couple brief; otherwise retain account-development status with no production forecast.

facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: AGC publicly markets destination-wedding planning and travel design, and names A’yesha as its planner/travel designer.

AGC explicitly requests group options and availability and manages the booking lifecycle; its published process places contract review before the client signs.
Spice Island independently advertises weddings for up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planning, catering and wedding/honeymoon packages.
AGC publicly identifies Breathless Getaways as its host agency; that agency identifies Adrienne Brown as its owner and offers owner-level advisor support.
uncertainties: No specific client programme, date, live proposal, confirmed block or historical Spice Island production was established in the reviewed sources.
A’yesha’s sourcing responsibility is explicit, but delegated signing authority, purchasing authority and who bears contractual liability remain unverified.
Adrienne’s role in any AGC Spice Island transaction, agency credentials used, and property-specific commercial terms require direct confirmation.
No named resort wedding/group account manager responsible for AGC was established; Debbie is a verified UK sales/referral route, not evidence of that assignment.
Actual guest affordability, suite availability, accessibility suitability and conversion probability cannot be established from destination marketing.
General references to corporate travel or past event experience do not establish current Spice Island corporate-meetings or incentive demand.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Develop the intermediary account first: contact A'yesha through the published AGC inbox, reference her firsthand Spice Island review, and ask whether she has an active Grenada couple brief or is building future destination recommendations. Offer a short trade/wedding qualification call and a current resort wedding/group fact sheet, using resort reservations to identify the correct account handler. Clarify her own sourcing role versus host-agency processing and client signature. Only after a live brief exists, request date/category availability and written group/wedding terms, obtain client approval and required agreement/deposit, issue booking instructions, and track pickup through delivery. Create one linked child programme per genuine couple brief; otherwise retain account-development status with no production forecast.

AGC’s Grenada page says A’yesha personally toured every listed resort, including Spice Island; the page also lists alternative Grenada properties.
A’yesha’s Spice Island review explicitly separates the resort’s property/setup/catering role from her own guest block, travel, design, timeline and welcome-party responsibilities.
AGC explicitly requests group options and availability and manages the booking lifecycle; its published process places contract review before the client signs.
Spice Island independently advertises weddings for up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planning, catering and wedding/honeymoon packages.
AGC publicly identifies Breathless Getaways as its host agency; that agency identifies Adrienne Brown as its owner and offers owner-level advisor support.
uncertainties: No specific client programme, date, live proposal, confirmed block or historical Spice Island production was established in the reviewed sources.
A’yesha’s sourcing responsibility is explicit, but delegated signing authority, purchasing authority and who bears contractual liability remain unverified.
Adrienne’s role in any AGC Spice Island transaction, agency credentials used, and property-specific commercial terms require direct confirmation.
No named resort wedding/group account manager responsible for AGC was established; Debbie is a verified UK sales/referral route, not evidence of that assignment.
Actual guest affordability, suite availability, accessibility suitability and conversion probability cannot be established from destination marketing.
General references to corporate travel or past event experience do not establish current Spice Island corporate-meetings or incentive demand.

recommended_next_step.body: Develop the intermediary account first: contact A'yesha through the published AGC inbox, reference her firsthand Spice Island review, and ask whether she has an active Grenada couple brief or is building future destination recommendations. Offer a short trade/wedding qualification call and a current resort wedding/group fact sheet, using resort reservations to identify the correct account handler. Clarify her own sourcing role versus host-agency processing and client signature. Only after a live brief exists, request date/category availability and written group/wedding terms, obtain client approval and required agreement/deposit, issue booking instructions, and track pickup through delivery. facts_and_uncertainties.title: Established facts and uncertainties
facts: AGC publicly markets destination-wedding planning and travel design, and names A’yesha as its planner/travel designer.
AGC’s Grenada page says A’yesha personally toured every listed resort, including Spice Island; the page also lists alternative Grenada properties.
A’yesha’s Spice Island review explicitly separates the resort’s property/setup/catering role from her own guest block, travel, design, timeline and welcome-party responsibilities.
AGC explicitly requests group options and availability and manages the booking lifecycle; its published process places contract review before the client signs.
Spice Island independently advertises weddings for up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planning, catering and wedding/honeymoon packages.
AGC publicly identifies Breathless Getaways as its host agency; that agency identifies Adrienne Brown as its owner and offers owner-level advisor support.
uncertainties: No specific client programme, date, live proposal, confirmed block or historical Spice Island production was established in the reviewed sources.
A’yesha’s sourcing responsibility is explicit, but delegated signing authority, purchasing authority and who bears contractual liability remain unverified.
Adrienne’s role in any AGC Spice Island transaction, agency credentials used, and property-specific commercial terms require direct confirmation.
No named resort wedding/group account manager responsible for AGC was established; Debbie is a verified UK sales/referral route, not evidence of that assignment.
Actual guest affordability, suite availability, accessibility suitability and conversion probability cannot be established from destination marketing.
General references to corporate travel or past event experience do not establish current Spice Island corporate-meetings or incentive demand.
